accepted.what: UNTESTED, not proven bugs: weekly/custom period_key, soft-deleted-account stops, unstaged prospects, stale-vs-active stage mismatch. Fixture has no row exercising any of them.
accepted.fix: Add fixture rows (weekly+custom cycle, soft-deleted account with a stop, soft-deleted prospect_stage, non-active-stage never-visited account) and assert the intended counts before changing SQL.
accepted.evidence: Block SQL with and without each proposed filter returns identical counts on repos_test_lexington: 1 trip stop, prospects 2=2, active 3 / stale 3, only cycle is monthly '2026-07'.

accepted.what: bigint ids go through Number() and round above 2^53, so a deep-link href built from the rounded value would 404 while the raw string id was in hand.
accepted.fix: Keep ids as strings in the contract and build hrefs from the raw string (upcomingTrips.ts:116 already does).
accepted.evidence: Node: Number('9007199254740995') -> 9007199254740996; pg returns bigint as string, so the raw value was available.

accepted.what: coverage runs 1+N serial queries (one per active cycle); statement_timeout is per statement, so worst-case latency scales with cycle count and no bound caps the block.
accepted.fix: Collapse the per-cycle loop into one set-based query joining cycles to the eligible/covered subqueries, with period_key passed as an array or computed per row.
accepted.evidence: Read coverage.ts: cycles query then an awaited counts query inside the for-loop; statement_timeout applies per statement only.

accepted.what: meeting_types ordered by `key`, a seed-only field; rep-created types (key NULL) always sort last, and sort_order/active are ignored entirely.
accepted.fix: ORDER BY sort_order, name and either filter inactive rows or expose `active` on MeetingTypeSummary.
accepted.evidence: SELECT id,key,name,active,sort_order FROM meeting_types on the fixture: sort_order 1-5 present, active present; neither is read by the query.

accepted.what: NEW: readMeetingTypes casts raw rows to MeetingTypeSummary, so bigint id is emitted as a string while the shared contract declares id: number. Live payload violates the contract.
accepted.fix: Map the rows explicitly (id: Number(row.id), or keep id as a string in MeetingTypeSummary) so /api/sources matches packages/shared/src/api.ts.
accepted.evidence: GET /api/sources on the running API returned meetingTypes [{"id":"3",...}]; packages/shared/src/api.ts:99 declares id: number.

accepted.what: One Promise.all under one try/catch: any block error blanks all five blocks, and a SQL typo or a pool-acquire timeout degrades a source with the same wording as a real outage.
accepted.fix: Settle the five block promises independently; classify pg codes (42703/42P01) and acquire timeouts separately from unreachable, log query errors at error level, keep HTTP 200 per-source degrade.
accepted.evidence: Pool probe with max 5: the 6th and 7th concurrent queries rejected with 'timeout exceeded when trying to connect', which buildOne's catch turns into degradedSource().

accepted.what: No in-flight dedup or negative caching, so N concurrent requests fire N probes at a down source; and only 'unreachable' is ever rechecked, so a behind/unknown recheck latches until restart.
accepted.fix: Memoize the in-flight recheck promise per source with a short cooldown (10-30s), and re-validate every status on a TTL so a recovered source is promoted back.
accepted.evidence: ensureSchemaCurrent returns early unless status==='unreachable' and holds no promise cache; each call issues its own checkSourceSchema query.

accepted.what: Health verdict ignores schemaStatus; latencyMs starts after the recheck/acquire; timezone and meetingTypes failures are swallowed into plausible defaults.
accepted.fix: Fold schemaStatus into the verdict (anything not ok/ahead is degraded), time from the start of the probe, and surface a null timezone or error field instead of DEFAULT_TIMEZONE/[].
accepted.evidence: Live /api/sources on an unreachable source returned schemaStatus 'unreachable' with timezone 'America/Chicago' and meetingTypes []; status is computed from `reachable` alone.

accepted.what: No request-level or per-source deadline anywhere; statement_timeout bounds one statement, so a slow source multiplies it by the number of serial statements.
accepted.fix: Add a per-request deadline around buildToday and a per-source budget inside buildOne, degrading the source that overruns.
accepted.evidence: routes/today.ts awaits buildToday with no timeout; pg applies statement_timeout per statement (node_modules/pg/lib/client.js:558).

accepted.what: The nowOverride module global is guarded only by NODE_ENV==='production', which apps/api/src/index.ts never sets, so it is armed outside the Docker image; generatedAt ignores it.
accepted.fix: Per the owner decision, inject `now` via createServer options instead of a module global, and derive generatedAt from that same instant.
accepted.evidence: index.ts sets no NODE_ENV (only Dockerfile:39 does); setNowOverrideForTests throws only when NODE_ENV==='production'.

accepted.what: Redaction matches only scheme://user:pass@host, so a DSN carrying ?password= or a keyword DSN reaches a 500 body or a log line unredacted.
accepted.fix: Also strip password=/PGPASSWORD= key-value pairs in query strings and keyword DSNs before returning the message.
accepted.evidence: Ran CREDENTIAL_SHAPED on 'postgresql://127.0.0.1:5432/db?password=S3cr3t': returned unchanged.

accepted.what: Per-source max is hard-clamped to 5 by Math.min while one request fires 5 block queries in parallel, so two concurrent requests to one source already queue behind the acquire timeout.
accepted.fix: Allow a configurable per-source max (or bound blocks in flight to 2-3 in services/today.ts) so normal concurrency cannot exhaust the pool.
accepted.evidence: Probe with max 5: 5 concurrent pg_sleep(4) succeeded, the 6th and 7th failed with 'timeout exceeded when trying to connect'.

accepted.what: createSourcePoolFactory is an unused export that drops both timeout options, and schema.ts holds a second, unexported, untested copy of the credential regex that can silently diverge.
accepted.fix: Delete createSourcePoolFactory (or pass the same bounded defaults), and export one redactMessage from @repos/sources with a unit case covering it.
accepted.evidence: grep for createSourcePoolFactory finds only its declaration; grep 'redact' in packages/sources/src/*.test.ts returns no hits.

accepted.what: The pool 'error' listener logs raw (err as Error).message, the only error sink that bypasses redaction, directly contradicting its own comment; nothing tests the claim.
accepted.fix: Route the message through the shared redaction helper before console.error and add a test that a credential-shaped message is scrubbed.
accepted.evidence: Read the listener: console.error interpolates the raw message; grep 'redact' in packages/sources/src/pool.ts returns nothing.

accepted.what: rejectCredentialShaped rejects any name containing password/secret/token, so a venture named e.g. 'Token Furniture' makes sources.json unloadable; a webUrl with a trailing slash is kept verbatim.
accepted.fix: Apply the keyword check to slug/webUrl only (or require a key=value shape), and strip trailing slashes from webUrl in parseSourcesFile.
accepted.evidence: Regex /password|secret|token/i is applied to entry.name; 'http://pathfinder.local:3000/' + '/accounts/48' yields a double slash.

accepted.what: The shipped bundle bakes an absolute base http://127.0.0.1:3200, which Caddyfile.example's connect-src 'self' blocks, and the Docker build cannot override it (no ARG, .env dockerignored).
accepted.fix: Default API_BASE_URL to '' so every call is same-origin /api/*, per the owner's Caddy decision.
accepted.evidence: grep -o 'http://127.0.0.1:[0-9]*' apps/web/dist/assets/*.js returns the literal once; grep ARG Dockerfile returns nothing.

accepted.what: apiGet casts the response to T with no validation and nothing catches a render error, so any API shape drift becomes a blank white page instead of an error state.
accepted.fix: Parse responses with zod (already a dependency in packages/sources) in apiGet, and wrap App in an ErrorBoundary that renders a recoverable message.
accepted.evidence: api.ts:34 returns (await res.json()) as T; no ErrorBoundary appears in main.tsx or App.tsx; data.sources.map throws when sources is absent.

accepted.what: isError is checked before data, so a failed background refetch discards good cached data and replaces the whole page with a raw error string.
accepted.fix: Render data whenever it is defined and show the error as a banner; fall back to the full-page error only when data is undefined.
accepted.evidence: Read TodayPage: the isError branch returns before the isPending and data branches; TanStack v5 keeps data defined on a failed refetch.

accepted.what: No h1 anywhere (headings start at h2/h3), no role/aria-live on the loading and error regions, and progress bars are bare divs with an inline width only.
accepted.fix: Add an h1 ('Today' plus the as-of timestamp), role=status/aria-live on loading and role=alert on errors, and role=progressbar with aria-valuenow/min/max and a label on both bars.
accepted.evidence: grep -rn 'role=|aria-|<h1' apps/web/src returns no matches at all.

accepted.what: Empty-state and metadata text uses text-slate-400 (#94a3b8) on white, about 2.6:1 at 14px, below the WCAG AA 4.5:1 minimum for body text.
accepted.fix: Use slate-600 or darker for empty-state and secondary text.
accepted.evidence: Read the four components: every empty state and the timezone/periodKey spans carry text-slate-400 on the white page background.

accepted.what: sources: [] renders four zero tiles and nothing else, so an empty or fully failed config looks identical to a healthy zero day, and generatedAt is never shown.
accepted.fix: Render an explicit 'No sources configured' state and show generatedAt as a visible 'as of' line in the header.
accepted.evidence: Read TodayPage: TotalsHeader then data.sources.map with no empty branch; generatedAt is not referenced anywhere in apps/web/src.

accepted.what: refetchOnWindowFocus is false with no staleTime, no refetchInterval and no refresh control, so an open Today tab never updates.
accepted.fix: Per the owner decision: 60s refetchInterval with 30s staleTime, plus a visible 'as of' timestamp in the header.
accepted.evidence: main.tsx sets defaultOptions { refetchOnWindowFocus: false, retry: 1 } only; TodayPage's useQuery passes just queryKey and queryFn.

accepted.what: fetch is issued with no AbortSignal or timeout and the client retries once, so a slow /api/today hangs the page and doubles load on an already saturated 5-connection pool.
accepted.fix: Pass AbortSignal.timeout(...) into apiGet/fetchToday and drop retry for this query.
accepted.evidence: grep for AbortSignal or signal in apps/web/src/lib/api.ts returns no matches; retry: 1 is set in main.tsx.

accepted.what: Up to 8 links per source share the accessible name 'Open in Pathfinder' (WCAG 2.4.4), and the e2e test selects it with .first(), so it pins row ordering rather than the intended row.
accepted.fix: Give each link aria-label={`Open ${row.name} in Pathfinder`} and select the e2e link inside the needs-visit-row-48 testid.
accepted.evidence: Read NeedsVisitBlock: the anchor text is a constant per row; e2e/today.spec.ts:28 calls .first() on getByRole('link', { name: 'Open in Pathfinder' }).

accepted.what: fetchSources/fetchHealth and queryKeys.sources/health have no consumers, the @web alias is unreferenced, and no test covers the page-level empty-sources state.
accepted.fix: Delete the unused exports and the alias (or use it), and add a TodayPage test for sources: [] asserting the new empty-state element.
accepted.evidence: grep across apps/web/src and e2e finds only the declarations of fetchSources/fetchHealth and no '@web/' import; no test file exists under apps/web.

accepted.what: env_file supplies REPOS_API_HOST=127.0.0.1, so the API binds container loopback while Docker publishes to the container's bridge IP; the mapped port is refused and Caddy never reaches the API.
accepted.fix: Per the owner decision, set REPOS_API_HOST=0.0.0.0 in the compose service environment only; the 127.0.0.1: host-side publish still restricts exposure.
accepted.evidence: index.ts:26 defaults HOST to 127.0.0.1 and reads REPOS_API_HOST; .env.example:17 ships 127.0.0.1 and compose loads .env via env_file.

accepted.what: The published mapping is '127.0.0.1:${REPOS_API_PORT:-3200}:3200' — the container side is hardcoded while the app listens on REPOS_API_PORT, and DEPLOY.md:62 invites changing that port.
accepted.fix: Use '127.0.0.1:${REPOS_API_PORT:-3200}:${REPOS_API_PORT:-3200}' so both sides move together.
accepted.evidence: Read the ports line verbatim; apps/api/src/index.ts:22 takes PORT from REPOS_API_PORT.

accepted.what: The docs tell Caddy to serve apps/web/dist from the host, but the bundle exists only inside the image and nothing extracts it; the vite-preview fallback names a 'web' service and port 5173 that do not exist.
accepted.fix: Add a named volume or bind mount for apps/web/dist (or document a docker cp / host build step), and either add a real web service with a published port or delete the fallback from both comment blocks.
accepted.evidence: docker-compose.yml declares one service, api, with no volumes key and no 5173 publish; vite.config.ts:20 binds preview to 127.0.0.1.

accepted.what: First-run step 2 never mentions REPOS_WEB_ORIGIN although the image sets NODE_ENV=production and the server throws at boot without it, so step 3 always fails.
accepted.fix: Add REPOS_WEB_ORIGIN=https://repos.<tailnet>.ts.net to the DEPLOY.md fill-in list and correct .env.example's loopback default (INT owns .env.example).
accepted.evidence: grep -rn REPOS_WEB_ORIGIN docs/ README.md returns nothing; server.ts:32-36 throws when it is unset and NODE_ENV==='production'.

accepted.what: §7 lists eight criteria while README and the tests say nine; §2.3 says a sources.json entry carries a read-only DATABASE_URL, contradicting §6, CLAUDE.md and the code; §4's field lists and §8's sources.example.json are stale.
accepted.fix: Sync §2.3 (slug/name/kind/webUrl, credential in .env), regenerate §4's lists from packages/shared/src/api.ts, add the ninth criterion from .orchestrator/state.md, and replace sources.example.json with sources.json.
accepted.evidence: Counted §7: exactly 8 numbered items; state.md line 76 says 'all nine criteria'; sources.json has no URL field; ls sources.example.json fails.

accepted.what: README points at DEPLOY.md for the fixture databases, but DEPLOY.md never mentions them; the real setup lives in test/fixtures/pathfinder/LOCAL_DB.md, which is excluded from the repo.
accepted.fix: Add a fixture/test-database section to DEPLOY.md (or point README at test/fixtures/pathfinder/README.md) and commit a non-secret LOCAL_DB template.
accepted.evidence: grep -i fixture docs/DEPLOY.md returns nothing; git ls-files shows test/fixtures/pathfinder/README.md but no LOCAL_DB.md.

accepted.what: Two documented guarantees overstate the code: the 'Trips this week' tile is week-overlap any-status while the list is start_date >= today, and default_transaction_read_only is a session default, not a lock.
accepted.fix: Per the owner decision, keep both behaviours and document them: state the two trip definitions in §3/§4, and describe the read-only session option as defense-in-depth behind the repos_reader grant.
accepted.evidence: SET default_transaction_read_only = off through a RepOS pool succeeded (current_setting returned 'off'); the two trip predicates differ as quoted.

accepted.what: The grant recipe never revokes TEMP from PUBLIC, so repos_reader can CREATE TEMP TABLE, and ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES silently grants SELECT on every future Pathfinder table, including one that may hold raw secrets.
accepted.fix: Add REVOKE TEMP ON DATABASE <db> FROM PUBLIC, repos_reader, and either drop the default-privileges line in favour of per-table grants or gate it on the schema-coupling bump.
accepted.evidence: As repos_reader on repos_test_lexington: CREATE TEMP TABLE t_probe(x int) succeeded and has_database_privilege(...,'TEMP') returned true.

accepted.what: file_server without try_files makes any deep link 404 before React loads, so App.tsx's catch-all redirect route is dead in the documented deploy.
accepted.fix: Add `try_files {path} /index.html` to the static block (or reverse_proxy the preview server instead).
accepted.evidence: grep -n try_files Caddyfile.example returns no matches; the static block is root + file_server only.

accepted.what: Number(env) yields NaN for a non-numeric value, and pg then drops BOTH bounds: the connect timeout falls back to 0 (disabled) and statement_timeout is never sent.
accepted.fix: Validate both env numbers at boot with Number.isFinite(n) && n > 0 and refuse to start otherwise.
accepted.evidence: node_modules/pg/lib/client.js:116 does `c.connectionTimeoutMillis || 0` then checks `> 0`; line 558 does `if (params.statement_timeout)` — NaN is falsy in both.

accepted.what: app.listen has no 'error' listener so EADDRINUSE becomes an uncaught exception, there is no SIGTERM/SIGINT handler, and the boot-failure catch sets exitCode without closing pools already opened.
accepted.fix: Attach server.on('error'), add a SIGTERM/SIGINT handler that closes the server then factory.close(), and hoist the factory so the catch can close it.
accepted.evidence: Read index.ts:56-65: listen takes only a callback; main().catch logs and sets process.exitCode with no close(); factory is scoped inside main().

accepted.what: The 500 handler returns errorMessage(err) as `detail` to unauthenticated callers; redaction strips only URL-shaped credentials, so hostnames, database names and relation names still reach the body.
accepted.fix: Log the detail server-side and return a generic detail, or include detail only when NODE_ENV !== 'production'.
accepted.evidence: Read server.ts:56-62; redact.ts:13 matches only scheme://...@host, so a plain 'relation "x" does not exist' passes through untouched.

accepted.what: The env template still ships VITE_API_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3200, which reintroduces the cross-origin base after the same-origin fix, and apps/web declares date-fns and date-fns-tz although only apps/api imports them.
accepted.fix: Drop VITE_API_BASE_URL from .env.example (or document it as dev-only) and remove both date-fns packages from apps/web/package.json.
accepted.evidence: grep for date-fns across apps/web/src and e2e returns nothing; the only import is apps/api/src/blocks/upcomingTrips.ts, and apps/api declares both itself.

accepted.what: The Chromium executablePath defaults to a sandbox-only path with no fallback to Playwright's own resolution, and reuseExistingServer: !CI lets e2e reuse a dev API started from .env with real source credentials.
accepted.fix: Fall back to Playwright's default resolution when REPOS_E2E_CHROMIUM_PATH is unset (documenting the override), and set reuseExistingServer: false for the API server or give e2e its own port.
accepted.evidence: ls ~/.cache/ms-playwright fails (no such directory); the API webServer entry sets reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI while the web entry sets false.

accepted.what: The whole API bootstrap is uncovered: no test imports index.ts, and REPOS_API_HOST is never exercised with a non-default value.
accepted.fix: Extract host/port/timeout resolution into a small exported helper and unit-test it, including a non-default REPOS_API_HOST and a non-numeric timeout.
accepted.evidence: grep -rn REPOS_API_HOST across .ts files returns only index.ts:26; no test file imports apps/api/src/index.ts.

refuted.why: Explicit owner decision in the brief: keep users.id = 1. Fixture confirms a single live user with id 1 in both databases, so no current source is affected.

refuted.where: F10 — claimed reproduction: 20 concurrent /api/today gave 5/20 responses with zeroed totals
refuted.why: Did not reproduce: 20 concurrent GET /api/today against the healthy fixtures returned 20/20 HTTP 200 in ~0.15s with no error field. Only the acquire-timeout mechanism stands (accepted under F9,F10,F14).

refuted.where: F1 — claim that the weekly and custom period_key conventions are unverified
refuted.why: Partly refuted: vendored migrations 0025/0026 document '2026-W29' and '2026-07-21+6w#3', exactly what cyclePeriodKey emits. Only the #index base and ISO week-year edges remain unpinned.

Numbers not reproduced against a refused port: latencyMs was null for the unreachable source, 11ms for the live one, and the whole call took 0.03s. The exclusion of recheck/acquire cost is still real.

refuted.where: F13 — claim that a 'behind' source still yields health status 'ok'
refuted.why: Narrower than stated: boot refuses a behind/unknown source, so this is reachable only via a recheck that settles into behind/unknown. Accepted on that path, not as a boot-time state.

deferred.why: Byte-for-byte confirmation needs a session in the Pathfinder repo; the brief's isolation rule forbids reading /home/user/reptech-pathfinder from here. Park as a Pathfinder-side check.

deferred.why: A server-side change on each source database, not a change to any file this repo owns; belongs in the ops runbook alongside the grant recipe.

deferred.where: playwright.config.ts — removing the sandbox Chromium path outright
deferred.why: cdn.playwright.dev is blocked by sandbox egress, so the pinned path must stay as a fallback behind REPOS_E2E_CHROMIUM_PATH or e2e cannot launch in this environment.
No container runtime available in this sandbox, so F25/F52/F53 were verified from the exact config lines and the app's own bind/port logic rather than by running compose.

deferred.why: No browser available here; verified by reading the components and by grep (zero role/aria/h1 occurrences in apps/web/src), which is conclusive for presence but not for computed styles.
